**Solution 1 (answer 12): reject.** Its diamond argument fails. A diamond subdivision is a theta, so diamond-subdivision-free graphs are exactly theta-free graphs. Layered wheels (Sintiari–Trotignon) are triangle-free and theta-free with unbounded treewidth, and I believe they also have unbounded mim-width, hence unbounded clique-width. That would kill the diamond, so the claim that every block must be a clique or cycle is false. Its unit-interval kill of the claw is also wrong, since unit interval graphs have bounded clique-width. The claw is still killed by line graphs of walls, which are claw-free with unbounded clique-width.

**Solution 2 (answer 3): reject.** Its killing argument relies on unit interval graphs as an unbounded-clique-width family, which is false. It also removes the paw without a valid construction. I could not find an unbounded clique-width family in which every member contains an induced subdivision of the paw. For example, grids, line graphs of walls and complements of walls all contain paw subdivisions, and split graphs with no paw subdivision have a near-threshold structure that looks bounded. So the paw most likely belongs to $\mathcal M$, and the answer 3 is probably too small.

**Solution 3 (answer 7): accept, with moderate confidence.** Its structure seems right: $\mathcal M$ has only 4-vertex members, $P_4$ and the paw are the likely members, and $K_3+K_1$ (3 edges) cannot change the edge-count set. The diamond exclusion via layered wheels agrees with my reasoning. The paw step is unproven, and the answer rests on it, so my confidence is only moderate.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
